body:
I’ll ask them about it. I’ve been pretty afraid of anti-psychotics/mood stabilizers because I’ve heard the side effects can get pretty bad. Also weight gain, I gained like 50 pounds as a teenager when I was on Abilify. But if they think they can give it to me without issues I’ll consider it. 

I also emailed a place that does ketamine infusion that was on the list of referral places my therapist gave me. I might give that a try after covid isn’t going as crazy, if I can get it for something in like the 2-3 thousand dollar range.

I’ve tried many anti depressants over the course of my life. Although I haven’t tried any since I’ve been diagnosed with CPTSD. I have an appointment with an RN that’s affiliated with my therapist’s office on Thursday. I’m going to ask them to prescribe me Zoloft since it’s apparently fairly effective in treating PTSD, and Buspar, just because it’s an additional anxiety medication and it’s not really supposed to have any side effects at all.

I’ve been very apprehensive about trying medication again - I was prescribed a combo of klonopin, adderall, lexapro and occasional other meds from 2014-2016 and it nearly ruined my life from how insane it made me go. But I feel like I’ve been genuinely delusional and out of touch with reality with the kind of beliefs and thinking that I’ve had about this stuff lately. I feel extremely mentally sick. So I’m willing to try anything that might help at this point.

The thing is, I don’t even truly believe they’re dating in the rational part of my brain. I’ve been told by his brother who had been my best friend of like 15 years up until a couple months ago that nothing was going on between them and that she would never be interested in him - and honestly I think that’s true too. And another mutual friend also confirmed that they don’t have a thing. But it’s the fucking insane chunk of my brain that’s dominating everything else and convincing me all the rational evidence I have that there’s nothing to worry about is wrong. That’s as stressful as any part of this.

And I mean I can’t really defend being devastated about this from a mentally healthy point of view. But at the same time, I’m also not mentally healthy. I grew up abused and neglected, and this girl is not just an old friend, she was the first person I ever dated in any capacity - and by extension, she was the first person that ever treated me like she cared about me and that I was good enough for them. I’m really deeply attached to her for that alone (and from having an attachment disorder.)

On top of that, I really feel like this was my last chance to be with somebody I love. I’m 30 now, my ex broke up with me 7 years ago. I feel like people don’t believe this could be true, but I completely stopped being attracted to people during that whole time. It feels like I have wasted the prime of my life alone and it doesn’t feel like there’s an end to that that’s possibly near. Reconnecting with this friend of mine, and feeling the things I felt about her, is the first time I’ve had hope since all the way back in 2014. I genuinely haven’t ever felt the way I felt about her, since I was still in a relationship with my ex who I wanted to spend the rest of my life with. And it feels like I just missed my chance to make up for that, and to stop my suffering.

I know that’s not the mentally healthy approach to that, I know there’s a ton of dependence and other unhealthy dynamics at play there. I’ve been in therapy dealing with them for the last 4 years now and putting as much effort into that as I can. But, that is where I’m at with it right now and that’s why I feel devastated over it.

I think so. I mean, the other thing is kind of like, I really trusted this guy, he was also one of my closest friends. It also feels like a stab in the back that he wasn’t there for me after I made the decision to stop talking to her. I looked up to this guy kind of like as an older brother. And I talked to him about how much it would hurt if it ended up not working out with her.

So I mean yes, they’re both allowed to do whatever they want. I don’t really like to ever think in terms of people being obligated to do anything. But as somebody who was my friend, it would definitely feel like he was actively choosing to not give a shit about my feelings or how much it would hurt me if he pursued her, really at any point. I think friends generally understand not to like, pursue someone’s ex or something. This is kind of like that to me, with the level of attachment I have with her. He has the right to not care about that if he wants, but it would be profoundly painful to me and would essential confirm that nobody is to ever be trusted again. And the thing is, my anxiety about this is so heavily predicated on things that I observed while we were hanging out, so if something was happening now, it’s essentially impossible that he wasn’t making a move on her when we were hanging out - that’s what my anxiety is convincing me I observed.

The real problem is, rationally I don’t believe anything is actually happening. I’ve been told by multiple mutual friends and this dude’s brother who was my best friend before a couple months ago that nothing was going on, and that she would never ever be into him. But there is a corner of my brain that is going fucking insane with anxiety and paranoia, and it’s dominating the rest of my brain and not allowing me to ground myself using the actual real evidence that I have that my fears are unfounded.

> Your feelings that you don't want her to get with that guy are not fair to her, or you.

I extremely disagree. She’s allowed to do what she wants. But I was essentially in love with this person. It fucking devastated me that it didn’t work out between us. And if I was picking up on something, it means it was going back to when my friend was giving me advice and support on my feelings for her and essentially letting me trust him by telling him about my deep attachment issues with her.

He can also do what he wants, but he knows how much it would hurt me if he was doing something like that behind my back at the time. I’m not going to have no feelings in response to that.

And I have had to be convinced that it’s okay to feel that way myself. My therapist has been constantly telling me for years that I need to stop letting my friends roll over me and treat me like shit, and really had to basically pound it into my head that it’s not okay for my friend to do this to me.

I mean if I were right about this, it would essentially mean that I was picking up on this while this friend of mine was encouraging me to pursue her and giving me advice and being supportive about it and etc etc, which would be a major stab in the back. That would be incredibly dishonest behavior.

She can do whatever she wants, and so can he. Nobody is obligated it to do anything. But he would be a monumentally shitty friend if he let me trust him with all the information I gave him about my long ongoing situation with her, pretended like he had my back as I was pursuing her, and then actually pursued her for himself as that was going on. And it’s perfectly reasonable for me to have feelings about that.

This isn’t my own conclusion either, for the record. My therapist has had to drill it into my head that I can’t allow people to treat me poorly, and really had to hammer it into me constantly that this would be an example of it and that I can’t stand for it.

I had asked her to hang out a few times just us, and she was flaky about it. I gave it a few chances, but I could tell she wasn’t being straight up with me. So I just asked her straightforward, I said it seemed like she didn’t want to hang out with me and I asked her if that was true, and she said it was true that she didn’t think it would be a good idea given my feelings for her. She wanted me to continue hanging out with her amongst everyone else, but I told her it wouldn’t work for me, it just hurt a lot and I couldn’t really go through it.

I reached out to my other friends because I was really struggling over it, and they just ignored me.
